name: Honda Aero, Inc. (GE Honda HF120 engines) - Burlington NC

fieldNotes.siteIdentity: Honda Aero, Inc. at 2989 Tucker St, Burlington NC — the GE Honda HF120 turbofan engine assembly/test plant adjacent to Burlington-Alamance Regional Airport. Confirmed: a single large modern white-roof manufacturing building (~132,000 sq ft after the 2016/2017 50,000 sq ft expansion) with an aircraft apron facing the runway. Verified by 2026 Street View showing the modern facility on Tucker St and z19-z20 satellite. The roster coordinates (movedMeters 36) sat on the airport apron just east of the building; coords were tightened onto the building center.
fieldNotes.facilityNature: This is a jet-engine ASSEMBLY and test plant, not a freight/distribution facility. Truck activity is minimal (small inbound parts shipments). There are no trailer drop yards and only a few service dock doors. The dominant 'yard' is the airside aircraft apron, irrelevant to a truck-yard engagement.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck gate. The vehicle entrance off Tucker St is an open landscaped driveway into the employee parking lot — no barrier arm, no booth, no checkpoint. The chain-link fencing seen in Street View is the airport perimeter fence, not a Honda Aero truck-gate control. Classified false.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth observed at the entrance driveway in 2026 Street View or satellite.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — there is no truck gate at all.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: The short open driveway from Tucker St to the parking lot would hold at most 1-2 vehicles.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 0-10 — only a handful of service/parts dock doors at the building; no regular bank of loading bays. Honest overhead estimate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: NONE — no marked trailer drop stalls; no trailer drop operation.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Single building; the nearby buildings are separate airport tenants, not part of Honda Aero.
fieldNotes.railServed: False — no rail spur; served by road and the adjacent airfield.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural — the site is at the edge of a small regional airport surrounded by farmland and light development; 2026 Street View shows a rural two-lane road.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~14 acres for the Honda Aero parcel (building plus parking and apron frontage); the perimeter box is a best estimate as the parcel blends into the airport grounds.
